THE INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ACT, CHAPTER 131

THE Collective Agreement entered into between Tal Lanka Hotels PLC, No. 25, Galle Face Center Road, Colombo 03 of the one part andEmployee Relation and Staff Welfare Association of Tal Lanka Hotels PLC, Colombo of the other part on 01st day of April 2016 is herebypublished in terms of Section 06 of the Industrial Disputes Act, Chapter 131, of the Legislative Enactments of Ceylon (Revised Edition 1956).
M. D. C. AMARATUNGA,Commissioner of Labour.
Department of Labour,Labour Secretariat,Colombo 05.11th October, 2016.
Collective Agreement No. 20 of 2016
COLLECTIVE AGREEMENT

This Collective Agreement is entered into between, TAL LANKA HOTELS PLC, a duly incorporated company having its Registered Officeat No. 25, Galle Face Center Road, Colombo 3 (hereinafter referred to as the “EMPLOYER”) of the One part and the employees in the Non-Executive grades who are members of the EMPLOYEE RELATION AND STAFF WELFARE ASSOCIATION OF TAL LANKAHOTELS PLC, Colombo and whose names are stipulated in schedule one (1) hereof, (hereinafter referred to as “EMPLOYEES “ ) and whohave authorized Eleven employees, whose names are stipulated in the schedule Two (2) hereof (hereinafter referred to as “The AuthorizedBargaining Agents”), to represent their interests, agree and sign on their behalf, of the other Part,
WITNESSETH and it is hereby agreed between the parties as follows :
TITLE : This Collective Agreement shall hereinafter be known as the Tal Lanka Hotels PLC Non Executive Grades Collective Agreement2016 - 2018

1.Parties Covered and Bound.– The terms of this Collective Agreement shall cover and bind the Employer, the Employees who aremembers of the Employee Relation and Staff Welfare Association employed by the Employer in non-executive grades and whose namesappear in schedule one (1) hereof and The Authorized Bargaining Agents whose names appear in Schedue Two (2) hereof.

2.Date of Operation and Duration.– The Agreement shall be effective as from the First day of April 2016 and shall continue tobe in force thereafter unless it is terminated by either party giving one month’s notice in writing to the other, subject to the proviso that oneparty hereto shall not give such notice to the other party to commence before 1st of March 2018 and such notice shall not expire before 31stMarch 2018.
3.Salaries.– Parties agree that the basic wage of Employees covered by this Agreement shall be revised in the following manner:

(i).The Employees who have completed a minimum period of one year in service as at 1st April 2016 and who are in service as atthe date of singing of this Agreement will be entitled to the salary increase granted hereunder.
(ii).With effect from 1st April 2016 the monthly salaries of Employees will be revised in the following manner.

•Employees who have completed 01 year and less than 05 years - Rs. 1,900.00•Employees who have completed 05 years and less than 09 years - Rs. 2,900.00•Employees who have completed 09 years and above - Rs. 4,000.00
(iii).Parties agree that the above salary increase granted will cover a period of two years commencing with effect from 1st April2016 and ending on 31st March 2018.

(iv).The Employees entitled to the salary increase referred to above will be paid a sum of Rs. 3,800/-, or Rs.5,800/- or Rs.8,000/-as per 3 (iii) above as arrears for the period 1st April 2016 to 31st May 2018.
(v).The next Wage Settlement will be due on 1st April 2018.
4.Annual Increment.– The Employer will continue to grant the annual increment following the hitherto prevailed practice based onthe Performance management system.
GradePercentageRemarksA+15%Outstanding PerformerA12%Good PerformerB10%Average PerformerC8%Poor Performer
It was agree to take the number of no pays into consideration when deciding on the grading of individual based on their appraisals. Incrementswill be paid on Basic Salary.
No Pay:01 to less than 05 days= 6%:05 Days and Above= 0%

Special consideration will be made while awarding increments for those employees who are retiring in that particular Financial Year.Employee’s who are in the carder as at 01st October 2015 will only be considered for the increments.

5.Demands of a Financial Nature.– ‘‘The Bargaining Agents’’ and the ‘‘Employees’’ jointly and severely agree that they shall notmake any demands of a financial nature or any request in respect of matters covered by the Collective Agreement, during the initial period ofcoverage of this Collective Agreement and shall not resort to any form of trade union action on such matters during the said period. (The periodbetween 1st April 2016 to 31st March 2018)

6.Loans.– The employer will disburse ten loans per month to ten suitable employees following the practice hitherto prevailed andthe amount of each loan shall not exceed Rs. 100, 000/=.Such loans shall be granted only if the particular employee seeking the loan satisfiesthe eligibility criteria introduced by the employer.It is agreed between the parties that an employee who obtains such a loan shall not be entitledto any salary advance or any other loan or financial facility from the employer until such loan is fully settled by the employee.The loan shall berecovered in 10 monthly installments.

7.New Year Gift.– The employer will pay the annual New Year Gift following the hitherto prevailed practice, depending on thefinancial performance and profitability of the employer.The Employees through their Bargaining Agents may express their views for theconsideration of the Employer, prior to payment is made to the employees. New Year Gift wil be paid as per the company policy.
7.1No Pay for New Year Gift. –

(i).Authorized no pay upto 02 months subject to Medical Certificate will be paid and if it exceeds more than 02 months, bonus willbe calculated on pro rata basis.Ex : 03 months for approved no pay ( bonus amount/12) * 09 months.
(ii).Authorized no pay more than 03 months will not be entitled for New Year Gift amount.
(iii).This policy (No. 7.1) (i) & (ii) will not be applicable for those who are enjoying maternity benefits.

(iv).For unauthorized no pay, New Year Gift will be paid as follows,Ex: 01 Unauthorized no pay - 10% will be deducted from the New Year Gift 02 Unauthorized no pay - 20% will be deducted from the New Year Gift 05 Unauthorized no pay - 50% will be deducted from the New Year Gift 10 Unauthorized no pay - 100% will be deducted from the New Year Gift
(v).New Year Gift policy is as follows :
(i) Employees who are in the carder as at 31st December of the previous year will be entitled for a full New Year Gift amount.
(ii) Employees who are in the carder between 01st January - 30th June will be entitled to 50% from the New Year Gift.
(iii) Employees who are in the carder between 01st July - 30th September will be entitled to 25% of the New Year Gift amount.

(iv) Employees who joined after 1st October and above will not be entitled to a New Year Gift.8.Salary Advance. – The Employer will continue to grant salary advances for employees shall not exceed Rs. 7,000/=. The salaryadvance shall be recovered in monthly emoluments of the employees.

9.Death Donation.– The hitherto adopted practice regarding the Death Donation will continue. In the event of a death of a familymember of an employee, the joint death donation paid by the employer and employees to the employee concerned shall be Rs. 100,000/=. Inthe event of a death of an employee, the Employer and fellow employees jointly shall contribute an amount equal to Rs.200,000/=. Theemployer shall provide a vehicle to employees of the department to which the deceased employee was attached to, in order to attend thefuneral.The employer agrees that the facility of providing transport shall be applicable for even in the case of a death of a family member of anemployee.
10.Medical (Hospitalization).– Employer will continue the existing medical policy of the company and the employees are paidRs. 70,000/= per financial year.

11.Annual Day Outing.– The hitherto adopted practice regarding the Annual Day Outing entitl for staff will continue. Employermentshall grant Rs. 1000/= per employee in monetary value within a financial year.

12.Dispute Settlement Procedure.– The employees and the bargaining agents jointly and severally agree not to engage in any formof trade union action with regard to any matter covered by this Collective Agreement.With regard to matters not covered by this agreement theemployees and the bargaining agents agree to the following dispute settlement procedure:
(a)Whenever there is a dispute, a written statement of the dispute should be forwarded by the Bargaining Agent to the Employer, and

(c)If after the discussions, the matter cannot be resolved, the conciliatory proceedings under the Industrial Disputes Act No. 43 of
1950 (as amended) should be followed.

(d)If after conciliation has failed in the Labor Department, the employees wish to take trade Union action, written notice should begiven of not less than 14 days by the Bargaining Agents on behalf of the employees who are memebers of the EmployeeRelations and Staff Welfare Association to the Employer.
